newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng heading for 15,000 in 1997 - SocGen.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng heading for 15,000 in 1997 - SocGen.

text.p: Fair value for Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index will be found between 14,500 and 15,000 points this year, SocGen-Crosby Securities (HK) Ltd said on Tuesday.
"The outlook for growth in Hong Kong as we head into 1997 is bright," SocGen-Crosby economist Clive McDonnell told reporters.

Fair value for the Hang Seng would lie between 14,500 and 15,000 points and could hit 16,000 in the third quarter on optimism surrounding the British territory's handover to China at midnight on June 30, he said.
The blue-chip index closed at 13,548 on Tuesday, up 97 points.
McDonnell said the political risks associated with the handover were low.
"China will want to ensure a smooth transition of power with a view to boosting its standing in the international community," he said.
McDonnell said he recommends investors overweight their Hong Kong portfolios in property, banking, conglomerates and retail counters.
